q: A monk who always exerts himself with regard to the six lêsyâs, the six kinds of bodies, and the six (regular functions as) eating, will not stand, &c. (8)

s: mode of life is practised by Sramana (as a means of liberation)
q: A clever monk who always exerts himself with regard to the above-mentioned points, will soon be thoroughly released from the Circle of Births (21)

s: Sramana exerts himself with regard to six regular functions (always)
q: A monk who always exerts himself with regard to the six lêsyâs, the six kinds of bodies, and the six (regular functions as) eating, will not stand, &c. (8)

s: Sramana exerts himself with regard to seven rules of accepting alms (always)
q: A monk who always exerts himself with regard to the (seven) rules of accepting alms, and the seven causes of danger (to other men) will not stand, &c. (9)

s: Sramana exerts himself with regard to seven causes of danger (always; danger to other men)
q: A monk who always exerts himself with regard to the (seven) rules of accepting alms, and the seven causes of danger (to other men) will not stand, &c. (9)

s: Sramana exerts himself with regard to eight objects of pride (always)
q: A monk who always exerts himself with regard to the (eight) objects of pride, to that which protects his chastity, and to the tenfold Law of the monks. (10)

s: Sramana protects chastity (through exertion)
q: A monk who always exerts himself with regard to the (eight) objects of pride, to that which protects his chastity, and to the tenfold Law of the monks. (10)

s: Sramana exerts himself with regard to tenfold Law of the monks (always)
q: A monk who always exerts himself with regard to the (eight) objects of pride, to that which protects his chastity, and to the tenfold Law of the monks. (10)

s: Sramana exerts himself with regard to duties of the upâsakas (always; eleven duties)
q: A monk who always exerts himself with regard to the (eleven) duties of the upâsakas, and the (twelve) duties of the bhikshus, will not stand, &c. (11)

s: Sramana exerts himself with regard to duties of the bhikshus (always; twelve duties)
q: A monk who always exerts himself with regard to the (eleven) duties of the upâsakas, and the (twelve) duties of the bhikshus, will not stand, &c. (11)

s: Sramana exerts himself with regard to thirteen actions productive of Karman (always)
q: A monk who always exerts himself with regard to the (thirteen) actions (productive of Karman), to the various (fourteen) kinds of living beings, and the (fifteen) places of punishment of the wicked, will not stand, &c. (12)

s: Sramana exerts himself with regard to Living Beings (always; fourteen kinds)
q: A monk who always exerts himself with regard to the (thirteen) actions (productive of Karman), to the various (fourteen) kinds of living beings, and the (fifteen) places of punishment of the wicked, will not stand, &c. (12)

s: soul crosses Samsâra (by practising the mode of life)
q: I shall declare the mode of life that benefits the soul; by practising it many souls have crossed the ocean of Samsâra. (1)

s: Sramana exerts himself with regard to places of punishment of the wicked (always; fifteen places)
q: A monk who always exerts himself with regard to the (thirteen) actions (productive of Karman), to the various (fourteen) kinds of living beings, and the (fifteen) places of punishment of the wicked, will not stand, &c. (12)

s: Sramana exerts himself with regard to sixteen Gâthâs (always)
q: A monk who always exerts himself with regard to the sixteen Gâthâs, and to the (seventeen kinds of) neglect of self-control, will not stand, &c. (13)

s: Sramana exerts himself with regard to eighteen kinds of continence (always)
q: A monk who always exerts himself with regard to the (eighteen kinds of) continence, to the (nineteen) gñâtâdhyayanas, and the (twenty) cases for not concentrating one's thoughts, will not, &c. (14)

s: Sramana exerts himself with regard to gñâtâdhyayanas (always; nineteen)
q: A monk who always exerts himself with regard to the (eighteen kinds of) continence, to the (nineteen) gñâtâdhyayanas, and the (twenty) cases for not concentrating one's thoughts, will not, &c. (14)

s: Sramana exerts himself with regard to cases for not concentrating one's thoughts (always; twenty cases)
q: A monk who always exerts himself with regard to the (eighteen kinds of) continence, to the (nineteen) gñâtâdhyayanas, and the (twenty) cases for not concentrating one's thoughts, will not, &c. (14)

s: Sramana exerts himself with regard to twenty-two troubles (always)
q: A monk who always exerts himself with regard to the twenty-one forbidden actions, and the twenty-two troubles, will not stand, &c. (15)

s: Sramana exerts himself with regard to Sûtrakritâṅga (always; twenty-three lectures)
q: A monk who always exerts himself with regard to the twenty-three (lectures of the) Sûtrakritâṅga, and to the gods whose number exceeds by an unit (the number of the lectures of the Sûtrakritâṅga), will not stand, &c. (t 6)

s: Sramana exerts himself with regard to twenty-five clauses (always)
q: A monk who always exerts himself with regard to the twenty-five clauses, and (to the recitation of the twenty-six) chapters of the Dasâs, &c., will not stand, &c. (17)

s: Sramana exerts himself with regard to Dasâs (always; twenty-six chapters)
q: A monk who always exerts himself with regard to the twenty-five clauses, and (to the recitation of the twenty-six) chapters of the Dasâs, &c., will not stand, &c. (17)

s: Sramana exerts himself with regard to virtues of the laity (always; twenty-seven virtues)
q: A monk who always exerts himself with regard to the (twenty-seven) virtues of the laity, and the (twenty-eight lectures of the) Prakalpa, will not stand, &c. 08)

s: Samsâra is crossed by soul (through practice of the mode of life)
q: I shall declare the mode of life that benefits the soul; by practising it many souls have crossed the ocean of Samsâra. (1)

s: Sramana exerts himself with regard to Prakalpa (always; twenty-eight lectures)
q: A monk who always exerts himself with regard to the (twenty-seven) virtues of the laity, and the (twenty-eight lectures of the) Prakalpa, will not stand, &c. 08)

s: Sramana exerts himself with regard to causes of wrong knowledge (always; twenty-nine causes)
q: A monk who always exerts himself with regard to the (twenty-nine) causes of wrong knowledge, and the (thirty) causes of delusion, will not stand, &c. (19)

s: Sramana exerts himself with regard to causes of delusion (always; thirty causes)
q: A monk who always exerts himself with regard to the (twenty-nine) causes of wrong knowledge, and the (thirty) causes of delusion, will not stand, &c. (19)

s: Sramana exerts himself with regard to qualities of Siddhas (always; thirty-one qualities)
q: A monk who always exerts himself with regard to the (thirty-one) qualities of Siddhas, &c., the (thirty-two) Yogas, and thirty-three Âsâtanâs, will not stand, &c. (20)

s: Sramana exerts himself with regard to Yogas (always; thirty-two)
q: A monk who always exerts himself with regard to the (thirty-one) qualities of Siddhas, &c., the (thirty-two) Yogas, and thirty-three Âsâtanâs, will not stand, &c. (20)

s: Sramana exerts himself with regard to Âsâtanâs (always; thirty-three)
q: A monk who always exerts himself with regard to the (thirty-one) qualities of Siddhas, &c., the (thirty-two) Yogas, and thirty-three Âsâtanâs, will not stand, &c. (20)

s: Sramana is released from Samsâra (when clever and always exerting himself with regard to the stated points)
q: A clever monk who always exerts himself with regard to the above-mentioned points, will soon be thoroughly released from the Circle of Births (21)

s: tapas is practised by Sramana (in place of neglect of self-control)
q: One should desist from one thing, and practise another: desist from neglect of self-control, and practise self-control. (2)

s: love and hatred produces Karman (bad)
q: Love and hatred are two evils which produce bad Karman; if a monk always avoids them, he will not stand within the circle (of transmigration). (3)

s: love and hatred is avoided by Sramana (always)
q: Love and hatred are two evils which produce bad Karman; if a monk always avoids them, he will not stand within the circle (of transmigration). (3)

s: Karman is produced by love and hatred (bad)
q: Love and hatred are two evils which produce bad Karman; if a monk always avoids them, he will not stand within the circle (of transmigration). (3)

s: Sramana avoids love and hatred (always)
q: Love and hatred are two evils which produce bad Karman; if a monk always avoids them, he will not stand within the circle (of transmigration). (3)

s: final deliverance is a bliss
q: By the teaching of true knowledge, by the avoidance of ignorance and delusion, and by the destruction of love and hatred, one arrives at final deliverance which is nothing but bliss. (2)

s: ignorance and delusion is origin of desire
q: As the crane is produced from an egg, and the egg is produced from a crane, so they call desire the origin of delusion, and delusion the origin of desire. (6)

s: ignorance and delusion causes Karman
q: Love and hatred are caused by Karman, and they say that Karman has its origin in delusion; Karman is the root of birth and death, and birth and death they call misery. (7)

s: love and hatred is destroyed for final deliverance
q: By the teaching of true knowledge, by the avoidance of ignorance and delusion, and by the destruction of love and hatred, one arrives at final deliverance which is nothing but bliss. (2)

s: love and hatred is caused by Karman
q: Love and hatred are caused by Karman, and they say that Karman has its origin in delusion; Karman is the root of birth and death, and birth and death they call misery. (7)

s: desire is origin of ignorance and delusion
q: As the crane is produced from an egg, and the egg is produced from a crane, so they call desire the origin of delusion, and delusion the origin of desire. (6)

s: desire ceases on absence of greed
q: Misery ceases on the absence of delusion, delusion ceases on the absence of desire, desire ceases on the absence of greed, greed ceases on the absence of property. (8)

s: greed is origin of desire
q: Misery ceases on the absence of delusion, delusion ceases on the absence of desire, desire ceases on the absence of greed, greed ceases on the absence of property. (8)

s: greed ceases on absence of property
q: Misery ceases on the absence of delusion, delusion ceases on the absence of desire, desire ceases on the absence of greed, greed ceases on the absence of property. (8)

s: Karman is origin of love and hatred
q: Love and hatred are caused by Karman, and they say that Karman has its origin in delusion; Karman is the root of birth and death, and birth and death they call misery. (7)

s: Karman is root of birth and death
q: Love and hatred are caused by Karman, and they say that Karman has its origin in delusion; Karman is the root of birth and death, and birth and death they call misery. (7)

s: final deliverance is reached by right knowledge
q: By the teaching of true knowledge, by the avoidance of ignorance and delusion, and by the destruction of love and hatred, one arrives at final deliverance which is nothing but bliss. (2)

s: birth and death is a misery
q: Karman is the root of birth and death, and birth and death they call misery. (7)

s: Sramana is a monk (engaged in austerities)
q: A Sramana engaged in austerities, who longs for righteousness, should eat the proper quantity of allowed food, should select a companion of right understanding, and should live in a place suited to seclusion. (4)

s: Sramana longs for righteousness (while engaged in austerities)
q: A Sramana engaged in austerities, who longs for righteousness, should eat the proper quantity of allowed food, should select a companion of right understanding, and should live in a place suited to seclusion. (4)

s: Sramana eats allowed food (the proper quantity)
q: A Sramana engaged in austerities, who longs for righteousness, should eat the proper quantity of allowed food, should select a companion of right understanding, and should live in a place suited to seclusion. (4)

s: Sramana selects companion of right understanding
q: A Sramana engaged in austerities, who longs for righteousness, should eat the proper quantity of allowed food, should select a companion of right understanding, and should live in a place suited to seclusion. (4)

s: Sramana lives in seclusion (a place suited to)
q: A Sramana engaged in austerities, who longs for righteousness, should eat the proper quantity of allowed food, should select a companion of right understanding, and should live in a place suited to seclusion. (4)

s: Sramana avoids foolish people (throughout)
q: This is the road to it: to serve the Gurus and the old (teachers), to avoid throughout foolish people, to apply oneself earnestly to study, and to ponder zealously on the meaning of the Sûtras. (3)

s: Sramana applies oneself to study (earnestly)
q: This is the road to it: to serve the Gurus and the old (teachers), to avoid throughout foolish people, to apply oneself earnestly to study, and to ponder zealously on the meaning of the Sûtras. (3)

s: Sramana ponders the meaning of the Sûtras (zealously)
q: This is the road to it: to serve the Gurus and the old (teachers), to avoid throughout foolish people, to apply oneself earnestly to study, and to ponder zealously on the meaning of the Sûtras. (3)

s: Sramana avoids pleasures (when living alone)
q: If he does not meet with a clever companion who surpasses or equals him in virtue, he should live by himself, abstaining from sins and not devoted to pleasures. (5)

s: final deliverance is reached by ignorance and delusion (through avoidance)
q: By the teaching of true knowledge, by the avoidance of ignorance and delusion, and by the destruction of love and hatred, one arrives at final deliverance which is nothing but bliss. (2)

s: Sramana subdues senses
q: The mind of those who always live in unfrequented lodgings, who eat low food, and who subdue their senses, will not be attacked by the foe, Love, who is vanquished as disease is by medicine. (12)

s: Sramana avoids women (as a chaste monk)
q: As it is not safe for mice to live near the dwelling of a cat, so a chaste (monk) cannot stay in a house inhabited by women. (13)

s: Sramana does not watch women (their shape, beauty, coquetry, laughter, prattle, gestures, and glances)
q: A Sramana, engaged in penance, should not allow himself to watch the shape, beauty, coquetry, laughter, prattle, gestures, and glances of women, nor retain a recollection of them in his mind. (14)

s: Sramana practices chastity (as meditation of the noble ones)
q: Not to look at, nor to long for, not to think of, nor to praise, womankind: this is becoming the meditation of the noble ones, and it is always wholesome to those who delight in chastity. (15)

s: Sramana lives by himself solitude (as wholesome in every way)
q: Though those who possess the three Guptis, cannot be disturbed even by well-adorned goddesses, still it is recommended to monks to live by themselves, as this is wholesome in every way. (16)

s: Sramana should not fix his thoughts on the pleasant objects of the senses (when engaged in austerities)
q: A Sramana, engaged in austerities, who longs for righteousness, should not fix his thoughts on the pleasant objects of the senses, nor turn his mind from them, if they be unpleasant. (21)

s: Sramana removes faith (obstructions to)
q: The dispassionate man who has performed all duties will quickly remove the obstructions to right knowledge and to right faith, and whatever Karman produces obstruction (to righteousness). (108)

s: Sramana attains meditation and concentration of thoughts (when pure and free from hindrances)
q: Then he knows and sees all things, he is free from delusion and hindrances, his Âsravas have gone, and he is proficient in meditation and concentration of thoughts, and being pure he will arrive at beatitude when his life is spent. (109)

s: Gurus and the old (teachers) are served by Sramana
q: This is the road to it: to serve the Gurus and the old (teachers), to avoid throughout foolish people, to apply oneself earnestly to study, and to ponder zealously on the meaning of the Sûtras. (3)

s: righteousness is longs for Sramana
q: A Sramana engaged in austerities, who longs for righteousness, should eat the proper quantity of allowed food, should select a companion of right understanding, and should live in a place suited to seclusion. (4)

s: final deliverance is reached by love and hatred (through destruction)
q: By the teaching of true knowledge, by the avoidance of ignorance and delusion, and by the destruction of love and hatred, one arrives at final deliverance which is nothing but bliss. (2)

s: pleasures cause misery (through desire of pleasure)
q: From desire of pleasure arises the misery of the whole world, the gods included; whatever misery of body and mind there is, the dispassionate will put an end to it. (19)

s: pleasures are similar to Kimpâka (in their effect)
q: As the fruit of the Kimpâka is beautiful in taste and colour, when eaten; but destroys the life when digested, (being) poison; similar in their effect are pleasures. (20)

s: pleasures cause passions (in those attached to them)
q: Anger, pride, deceit, greed; disgust, aversion to self-control and delight in sensual things; mirth, fear, sorrow, carnal desire for women, men, or both; all these manifold passions arise in him who is attached to pleasures; and so do other emotions produced by those (before mentioned) arise in him who is to be pitied, who (ought to be) ashamed of himself, and who is hateful. (102, 103)

s: senses are fire like fire (when indulged through eating)
q: As in a forest, full of fuel, a fire fanned by the wind cannot be extinguished, so the fire (as it were) of the senses of him who eats as he lists; it does not benefit any chaste man. (11)

s: senses enslave one
q: Such emotions of an infinite variety arise in one who is the slave of his senses. (104)

s: women are difficult for Sramana (who longs for liberation)
q: To a man who longs for liberation, who is afraid of the Samsâra, and lives according to the Law, nothing in the world offers so many difficulties as women who delight the mind of the ignorant. (17)

s: women cause carnal desire (among manifold passions)
q: Anger, pride, deceit, greed; disgust, aversion to self-control and delight in sensual things; mirth, fear, sorrow, carnal desire for women, men, or both; all these manifold passions arise in him who is attached to pleasures; and so do other emotions produced by those (before mentioned) arise in him who is to be pitied, who (ought to be) ashamed of himself, and who is hateful. (102, 103)

s: Samsâra is feared by Sramana (who longs for liberation)
q: To a man who longs for liberation, who is afraid of the Samsâra, and lives according to the Law, nothing in the world offers so many difficulties as women who delight the mind of the ignorant. (17)

s: Samsâra contains misery (as a long succession of pains)
q: But a man who is indifferent to 'colours,' is free from sorrows; though still in the Samsâra, he is not affected by that long succession of pains, just as the leaf of the Lotus (is not moistened) by water. (34)

s: colour attracts the eye (when pleasant)
q: 'Colour' attracts the eye; it is the pleasant cause of Love, but the unpleasant cause of Hatred; he who is indifferent to them (viz. colours), is called dispassionate. (22)

s: misery is a affliction (of mankind)
q: He will get rid of all misery which always afflicts mankind; recovered from the long illness, as it were, and glorious, he becomes infinitely happy, and obtains the (final) aim. (110)

s: colour causes love and hatred (pleasantly or unpleasantly)
q: 'Colour' attracts the eye; it is the pleasant cause of Love, but the unpleasant cause of Hatred; he who is indifferent to them (viz. colours), is called dispassionate. (22)

s: colour is perceived by the eye
q: The eye perceives 'colour,' and 'colour' attracts the eye; the cause of Love is pleasant, and the cause of Hatred is unpleasant. (23)

s: colour causes ruin Sramana (when passionately desired)
q: He who is passionately fond of 'colours,' will come to untimely ruin; just as an impassioned moth which is attracted by the light rushes into death. (24)

s: colour causes pain Sramana (when passionately hated)
q: He who passionately hates (a colour), will at the same moment suffer pain. It is the fault of an undisciplined man that he is annoyed (by a colour); it is not the 'colour' itself that annoys him. (25)

s: colour is indifferent to Sramana (when dispassionate)
q: But a man who is indifferent to 'colours,' is free from sorrows; though still in the Samsâra, he is not affected by that long succession of pains, just as the leaf of the Lotus (is not moistened) by water. (34)

s: the mind is attacked by love and hatred (when attached to pleasures)
q: Anger, pride, deceit, greed; disgust, aversion to self-control and delight in sensual things; mirth, fear, sorrow, carnal desire for women, men, or both; all these manifold passions arise in him who is attached to pleasures; and so do other emotions produced by those (before mentioned) arise in him who is to be pitied, who (ought to be) ashamed of himself, and who is hateful. (102, 103)

s: the mind is indifferent to colour (when dispassionate)
q: A Sramana, engaged in austerities, who longs for righteousness, should not fix his thoughts on the pleasant objects of the senses, nor turn his mind from them, if they be unpleasant. (21)

s: the mind is proficient in meditation and concentration of thoughts (when pure)
q: Then he knows and sees all things, he is free from delusion and hindrances, his Âsravas have gone, and he is proficient in meditation and concentration of thoughts, and being pure he will arrive at beatitude when his life is spent. (109)

s: misery arises from birth and death
q: Karman is the root of birth and death, and birth and death they call misery. (7)

s: misery ceases on absence of ignorance and delusion
q: Misery ceases on the absence of delusion, delusion ceases on the absence of desire, desire ceases on the absence of greed, greed ceases on the absence of property. (8)

s: right knowledge leads to final deliverance
q: By the teaching of true knowledge, by the avoidance of ignorance and delusion, and by the destruction of love and hatred, one arrives at final deliverance which is nothing but bliss. (2)

s: ignorance and delusion is avoided for final deliverance
q: By the teaching of true knowledge, by the avoidance of ignorance and delusion, and by the destruction of love and hatred, one arrives at final deliverance which is nothing but bliss. (2)

q: The eight kinds of Karman are briefly the following: 1. Gñânâvaranîya (which acts as an obstruction to right knowledge); 2. Darsanâvaranîya (which acts as an obstruction to right faith); 3. Vêdanîya (which leads to experiencing pain or pleasure); 4. Môhanîya

s: Môhanîya leads to delusion
q: 4. Môhanîya (which leads to delusion);

s: Âyuhkarman is a Karman (one of the eight kinds)
q: The eight kinds of Karman are briefly the following: 1. Gñânâvaranîya (which acts as an obstruction to right knowledge); 2. Darsanâvaranîya (which acts as an obstruction to right faith); 3. Vêdanîya (which leads to experiencing pain or pleasure); 4. Môhanîya (which leads to delusion); 5. Âyuhkarman

s: Âyuhkarman determines length of life
q: 5. Âyuhkarman (which determines the length of life);

s: Antarâya is a Karman (one of the eight kinds)
q: The eight kinds of Karman are briefly the following: 1. Gñânâvaranîya (which acts as an obstruction to right knowledge); 2. Darsanâvaranîya (which acts as an obstruction to right faith); 3. Vêdanîya (which leads to experiencing pain or pleasure); 4. Môhanîya (which leads to delusion); 5. Âyuhkarman (which determines the length of life); 6. s: Antarâya prevents entrance on path that leads to eternal bliss
q: 8. Antarâya (which prevents one's entrance on the path that leads to eternal bliss).

q: 1. Obstruction of knowledge is fivefold

q: a. Sruta, knowledge derived from the sacred books;

s: Gñânâvaranîya obstructs perception
q: b. Âbhinibôdhika, perception;

s: Gñânâvaranîya obstructs supernatural knowledge
q: c. Avadhigñâna, supernatural knowledge;

s: Gñânâvaranîya obstructs knowledge of the thoughts of other people
q: d. Manahparyâya, knowledge of the thoughts of other people;

s: Gñânâvaranîya obstructs the highest, unlimited knowledge
q: e. Kêvala, the highest, unlimited knowledge.

q: The nine kinds of obstruction to right faith are: 1. sleep; 2. activity; 3. very deep sleep; 4. a high degree of activity; 5. a state of deep-rooted greed; 6-9 refer to faith in the objects of the first three and the last kinds of knowledge.

s: Vêdanîya is twofold pleasure and pain
q: 3. Vêdanîya is twofold, pleasure and pain;

s: Môhanîya is twofold faith and conduct (as referring to)
q: 4. Môhanîya is twofold as referring to faith and to conduct;

s: Môhanîya has subdivisions three (referring to faith)

s: Môhanîya has subdivisions two (referring to conduct)

s: Môhanîya refers to wrong faith (one kind of faith)
q: The three kinds of Môhanîya referring to faith are: 1. right faith; 2. wrong faith;

s: Môhanîya refers to faith partly right and partly wrong (one kind of faith)
q: The three kinds of Môhanîya referring to faith are: 1. right faith; 2. wrong faith; 3. faith partly right and partly wrong.

s: Môhanîya is experienced in the form of four cardinal passions (one kind referring to conduct)
q: The two kinds of Môhanîya referring to conduct are: 1. what is experienced in the form of the four cardinal passions;

s: Môhanîya is experienced in the form of feelings different from them (one kind referring to conduct)
q: 2. what is experienced in the form of feelings different from them.

s: Âyuhkarman is fourfold four (as referring to kinds of beings)
q: 5. Âyushka is fourfold as referring to 1. denizens of hell; 2. brute creation; 3. men; 4. gods.

s: Âyuhkarman refers to denizens of hell (one of four kinds)
q: 5. Âyushka is fourfold as referring to 1. denizens of hell;

s: Âyuhkarman refers to brute creation (one of four kinds)
q: 2. brute creation;

s: Âyuhkarman refers to men (one of four kinds)
q: 3. men;

s: Âyuhkarman refers to gods (one of four kinds)
q: 4. gods.

s: Gñânâvaranîya obstructs right knowledge
q: 1. Gñânâvaranîya (which acts as an obstruction to right knowledge);

q: 8. Antarâya is fivefold as preventing: 1. gifts; 2. profit; 3. momentary enjoyment; 4. continuous enjoyment; and 5. power.

s: Antarâya prevents gifts
q: 8. Antarâya is fivefold as preventing: 1. gifts;

s: Antarâya prevents profit
q: 2. profit;

s: Antarâya prevents momentary enjoyment
q: 3. momentary enjoyment;

q: 4. continuous enjoyment;

q: The longest duration of Môhanîya is seventy Krores of Krores of Sâgarôpamâs, and the shortest a part of a muhûrta.

s: Darsanâvaranîya is a Karman (one of the eight kinds)
q: The eight kinds of Karman are briefly the following: 1. Gñânâvaranîya (which acts as an obstruction to right knowledge); 2. Darsanâvaranîya

s: Môhanîya has shortest duration a part of a muhûrta
